Latin word

coalēscō

coalēscō, coalēscere, coaluī, coalitum

verb, third conjugation, intransitive; with cum and the ablative, or in with the accusative

grow together; of peoples and groups, become one, integrate

In this lexicon

  • integrate

    the recommended word · classical · Sall. C. 6.2 (Lewis & Short); Liv. 2.48.1: ut cum Patribus coalēscerent animī plēbis (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • ut cum Patribus coalēscerent animī plēbis

    so that the feelings of the commons might merge with those of the senatorsLiv. 2.48.1 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for integrate

  • perficiam ut hunc A. Licinium nōn modo nōn sēgregandum, cum sit cīvis, ā numerō cīvium, vērum etiam, sī nōn esset, putētis asciscendum fuisse

    I shall make you think that Archias should not only not be cut off from the citizens, being one, but should have been admitted even if he were notCic. Arch. 2 fin. (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for integrate

    The new neighbours have fitted in with us easily.composed
